WMT.rationale: Walmart is a high-quality franchise with durable competitive advantages (wide moat, grocery leadership, rapidly scaling high-margin ecosystem businesses). However, the stock is extremely unattractive at current levels on all three pillars. Pillar 1 (Fundamentals): Revenue growth is solid at +5.8% YoY (Q3 FY26) and +7.3% YoY (Q1 FY27), but margins have compressed — net margin stepped down from 3.6% to 2.8% in mid-2025 and has stayed flat, operating margin declined from 4.1% (Q2) to 3.7% (Q3), and ROE fell from 25.2% to 21.6%. The Q1 FY27 earnings beat on revenue but management issued soft guidance (Q2 EPS $0.72-0.74 vs consensus $0.75, FY27 EPS $2.75-2.85 vs consensus $2.91-2.97), explicitly flagging fuel cost headwinds ($175M hit in Q1 alone, expected larger in Q2) and consumer exhaustion. The trajectory is adequate but deteriorating at the margin, with management itself signaling caution. Pillar 2 (Valuation): The stock trades at 49.1x trailing P/E (up from 33.0x a year ago — 49% multiple expansion) and 42-44x forward P/E, with an earnings yield of 2.0% sitting 245bps below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.45%. This is an extreme premium for a mature retailer with compressing margins. P/B has stretched from 8.3x to 10.6x. The market is paying more for less — multiple expansion has occurred against margin compression, not expansion. Pillar 3 (Near-term catalyst): The most recent earnings event (Q1 FY27, reported 2026-05-21) was a negative catalyst — the stock fell ~7-8% post-report despite a top-line beat, because guidance disappointed. There is no credible positive near-term catalyst; instead, the near-term path includes rising fuel costs, pharmacy regulatory pressure, fading tax refund tailwinds, and potential tariff uncertainty. The IEEPA tariff refund (~$2.4B) would be prioritized for price investment, not bottom-line improvement. All three pillars align bearishly: deteriorating margin trajectory, extreme valuation with negative equity risk premium, and a negative near-term catalyst event. The stock is priced for defensive perfection and any disappointment is punished severely.

Net margin stepped down from 3.6% to 2.8% in mid-2025 and has stayed flat; operating margin declined from 4.1% (Q2) to 3.7% (Q3)
ROE declined from 25.2% to 21.6% — a one-time step-down, not ongoing, but the lower level persists

CFO warned fuel headwind ($175M in Q1) expected larger in Q2; tax refund tailwinds fading

High-margin ecosystem businesses (advertising +37%, marketplace +50%, membership +27%) are genuine positives but already priced into the premium multiple
